title: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table (KS4 Chemistry)
subject: Chemistry
strapline: What atoms are made of and how the table is organised.
facts: An atom has a central nucleus containing protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral), surrounded by electrons (negative) in shells.
Atoms are neutral overall because the number of protons equals the number of electrons.
The atomic number is the number of protons; the mass number is protons + neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same protons but different numbers of neutrons.
The periodic table is arranged in order of atomic number.
Vertical columns are groups (elements with similar properties and the same number of outer electrons); horizontal rows are periods.
Group 1 are the reactive alkali metals; Group 7 the halogens; Group 0 the unreactive noble gases.

quick_quiz.q: What is the charge of a proton?
What does the atomic number tell you?

quick_quiz.a: an atom with the same protons but a different number of neutrons

teacher_tips: Keep atomic number (protons) vs mass number (protons+neutrons) crisp.
Link group number to number of outer-shell electrons.
Use electron-shell diagrams (2,8,8) to explain reactivity trends.
